Definitions have initializers, declarations don't.
hasDefinitiveInitializer - Whether the global variable has an initializer, and any other instances of the global (this can happen due to weak linkage) are guaranteed to have the same initializer.

detaileddescription.para: Note that if you want to transform a global, you must use hasUniqueInitializer() instead, because of the *_odr linkage type.
= global SomeType* null - Initializer is both definitive and unique.
= global weak SomeType* null - Initializer is neither definitive nor unique.
= global weak_odr SomeType* null - Initializer is definitive, but not unique.

briefdescription.para: hasUniqueInitializer - Whether the global variable has an initializer, and any changes made to the initializer will turn up in the final executable.
getInitializer - Return the initializer for this global variable.

detaileddescription.para: It is illegal to call this method if the global is external, because we cannot tell what the value is initialized to!

briefdescription.para: setInitializer - Sets the initializer for this global variable, removing any existing initializer if InitVal==NULL.

detaileddescription.para: The initializer must have the type getValueType().

briefdescription.para: replaceInitializer - Sets the initializer for this global variable, and sets the value type of the global to the type of the initializer.

detaileddescription.para: The initializer must not be null. This may affect the global's alignment if it isn't explicitly set.

briefdescription.para: If the value is a global constant, its value is immutable throughout the runtime execution of the program.

detaileddescription.para: Assigning a value into the constant leads to undefined behavior.
